sources.title: Josh Kirklin, Generalised second law beyond the semiclassical regime, arXiv:2412.01903v3
sources.locator: Complete paper; abstract and Introduction, §2.1, §§3.1–3.4, §§4.1–4.3, §§5.2–5.3, and §6 for the algebra construction, exact modified GSL proof, cutoff/semiclassical reduction, and stated limits.
sources.reading_extent: Complete 48-page PDF retrieved; abstract/Introduction and the relevant proof chain in §§2.1–4.3, cutoff limit in §§5.2–5.3, and limitations in §6 inspected.

contents.name: Abstract and §§1–2.1: modified GSL target and fixed-cut algebra isotony issue
contents.support: Provides a close comparison: the paper defines generalized entropy by a gauge-invariant von Neumann algebra and proposes a modified inequality beyond the semiclassical regime.
contents.limitations: The source's algebra entropy and modified free-energy bound are not identified with the local finite-regulator entropy sequence in this problem.

contents.name: §§3.1–3.4 and §§4.1–4.3: ordered dynamical-cut algebras and relative-entropy derivation
contents.support: The proof constructs gauge-invariant algebras for idealized dynamical cuts, conditions on their ordering to obtain isotony, and applies relative-entropy monotonicity to derive the exact modified inequality including the later-cut free energy.
contents.limitations: The framework is perturbative gravity with auxiliary idealized quantum-reference cuts and its specified gauge-invariant algebra; it supplies no map to every selected semiclassical Einstein-scalar solution or fixed local renormalization prescription.

contents.name: §§5.2–5.3 and §6: UV-cutoff semiclassical reduction and limitations
contents.support: The paper obtains an approximate leading-order identification with the usual area-plus-outside entropy, up to a state-independent constant, and recovers ordinary monotonicity only when the cut free-energy term is nonnegative under additional conditions.
contents.limitations: The paper explicitly uses idealized auxiliary cuts and leaves realistic cut models for future work; it does not establish regulator-independent convergence for the fixed-scheme finite-regulator definition used here.
